_comment: Canonical claims: rules this repo must state identically everywhere they are relied on. Each entry pins the EXACT phrasings that count as stating the claim; a carrier contains one or it does not. There is no condition/negation inference — #341 deleted it after 24 review rounds and 100 findings with no downward trend. Read check-claims.js's header before editing: it explains why a phrasing must be long enough that no `mustNotMatch` string contains it, which the guard enforces mechanically at load. Adding a legitimately reworded carrier means adding its wording here — that visible edit IS the design, not a workaround.

claims.why: A clean Codex rerun can arrive as a 👍 reaction or as an INLINE REVIEW-THREAD REPLY, and an inline reply never enters the comment list. A file that says only 'check the comments' sends a session to a gate it cannot clear. Round 35 of #294 found that narrowed form in nine files while the source said both — this claim's best case, and the reason it is pinned. The phrasings carry their connector ('so check …', 'predictable: check …') rather than the bare instruction: with the bare form, inverting automations.md to 'so never check …' PASSED, because a phrasing is a substring of its own negation. Measured on #341, not imagined. 2026-09-23 (owner ruling): the non-directive carriers repo-monitors.md, automations.md, ci-triage.md, cicd-setup.md were collapsed to pointers at `directives/git.md` → PR Lifecycle / `docs/standards/pr-mechanics.md` and dropped from `consumers`, so a restated copy is no longer locked in. 2026-10-12 (owner-approved audit R2/R3): CLAUDE.md's restatement became a pointer at git.md and left `consumers`, and every phrasing no tracked file still carried was removed rather than kept as dead wording.

claims.why: #336 defined the *unreachable-review test* — the one condition under which a session may take `codex-flagged` off by hand — and then spent three consecutive review rounds being shown a consumer that had dropped it. Round 4: the commit that INTRODUCED the name coined two aliases for it in the same breath. A NAME is undone by a suffix rather than by a clause, so each phrasing pins the character that follows it ('test.', 'test admits', 'test, and') — that boundary is what keeps 'tests', 'tester', 'testing' and 'test-cases' from counting as the name, and the mustNotMatch entries are exactly those four. ⚠️ Pinning the name cannot see the CONTENT of the rule; `unreachable-review-terminal-states` is the entry that does. 2026-09-23 (owner ruling): the non-directive carriers automations.md, ci-triage.md, cicd-setup.md, repo-monitors.md were collapsed to pointers at `directives/git.md` → PR Lifecycle / `docs/standards/pr-mechanics.md` and dropped from `consumers`, so a restated copy is no longer locked in. 2026-10-12 (owner-approved audit R2/R3): CLAUDE.md's restatement became a pointer at git.md and left `consumers`, and every phrasing no tracked file still carried was removed rather than kept as dead wording.

claims.why: #299 phase 2 moved the reasoning for global.md's Hosting & Deployment rules into docs/standards/hosting-mechanics.md and condensed the rules to one bullet each, so the rule to DELETE an unrepointed pages-retry.yml now stands in global.md as a single bullet beside a pointer. It is the one Hosting rule whose loss turns a missed alarm into an active harm: a retry still watching pages-build-deployment re-runs the rogue unfiltered deploy a visibility flip fires. A later trim that kept the pointer and dropped the bullet would pass every other check. Each phrasing runs to its sentence terminator; the workflow carriers state it in their header comment with a semicolon, and automations.md without 'merely'/'while', so each carrier's own wording is listed and none contains another.

claims.why: ci-notify resolves ONE open PR from a head SHA, else branch plus head-repo owner. The WEAK failure (no unique candidate, so it exits silently) is not the dangerous one and is stated separately in every carrier; the dangerous one is that even a UNIQUE match proves nothing, because a repository_dispatch run carries the DEFAULT-BRANCH SHA and can uniquely match an unrelated promotion PR, which then receives the comment. Every phrasing therefore keeps 'unique' behind its article: 'unique' is a SUBSTRING of 'non-unique', so a carrier regressing to the weak case while wearing the strong case's words would otherwise still count. A carrier can state it ANAPHORICALLY, in words no earlier phrasing reached and --derive therefore could not surface (#314): git.md's PR Lifecycle bullet states the consequence ('that unrelated PR is commented while the session that triggered the dispatch waits.'). git.md's neighbouring 'it uniquely resolves the one matching workflow_run.head_branch' is the lookup MECHANISM, not this warning, and is deliberately left untracked rather than pinned under this id — the response-is-not-a-verdict mistake of certifying a neighbouring rule. 2026-09-23 (owner ruling): the non-directive carriers cicd-setup.md, repo-monitors.md, ci-triage.md were collapsed to pointers at `directives/git.md` → PR Lifecycle / `docs/standards/pr-mechanics.md` and dropped from `consumers`, so a restated copy is no longer locked in. 2026-10-12 (owner-approved audit R2/R3): the CLAUDE.md and MAINTAIN-REPO-USER-INSTRUCTIONS.md restatements became pointers at git.md and left `consumers`; every phrasing no tracked file still carried was removed, with the two mustNotMatch entries that existed only to constrain them.

claims.why: The counterpart to the wake gap above: when a run could end without waking the session, the check-in is what keeps the PR from being abandoned mid-flight. Rounds 37 and 39 of #294 were both this claim failing to reach a consumer — round 39's was in wait-gate.sh, which states the rule twice and whose DELIVERED message is the copy that matters. Its carriers word it differently, which is why there is one phrasing per wording and why #341 abandoned trying to infer the shape. Each lowercase one carries its connector: with a bare 'arm the check-in whenever …', inverting CLAUDE.md to 'Never arm the check-in whenever …' PASSED, because ci-notify's lowercase wording matched inside the negation — one carrier's phrasing covering another carrier's inversion. 2026-09-23 (owner ruling): the non-directive carriers repo-monitors.md, ci-triage.md, cicd-setup.md were collapsed to pointers at `directives/git.md` → PR Lifecycle / `docs/standards/pr-mechanics.md` and dropped from `consumers`, so a restated copy is no longer locked in. 2026-10-12 (owner-approved audit R2/R3): CLAUDE.md's restatement became a pointer at git.md and left `consumers`, and every phrasing no tracked file still carried was removed rather than kept as dead wording.

consumers.why: This file states the rule TWICE — once in its explanatory header comment, once inside the echo the PreToolUse hook actually delivers. The delivered copy carries the most authority: it reaches a session unprompted, at the decision point. Round 39 of #294 was this claim missing here. The header says 'arms a check-in alongside it' and the message says 'ARM A CHECK-IN ALONGSIDE IT', so the phrasing pinned for this claim matches only the delivered form — verified on #341 by deleting the rule from the echo alone, leaving the header intact, and watching the guard go red.
